title: F5 AI Gateway: Govern, Secure, Optimize AI
description: Single control plane unifying Model Gateway, MCP Gateway, and AI Guardrails to govern, secure, and cut token spend by 30-60%.
content_summary: F5 AI Gateway provides an enterprise control plane that unifies Model Gateway, Model Context Protocol (MCP) Gateway, and AI Guardrails under a single policy model to govern every model, agent, and tool with zero application changes required. It reduces token spend by 30–60% using semantic and exact caching, smart routing, and GPU-aware routing, while enforcing per-team budgets, token metering, and attribution. External Engineering, Protocols & Tools — Kubernetes, Containers & Cloud Native) details: Share a Cluster with Namespaces This page shows how to view, work in, and delete namespaces . The page also shows how to use Kubernetes namespaces to subdivide your cluster. Before you begin Have an existing Kubernetes cluster . You have a basic understanding of Kubernetes Pods , Services , and Deployments . Viewing namespaces List the current namespaces in a cluster using: kubectl get namespaces NAME STATUS AGE default Active 11d kube-node-lease Active 11d kube-public Active 11d kube-system Active 11d Kubernetes starts with four initial namespaces: default The default namespace for objects with no other namespace kube-node-lease This namespace holds Lease objects associated with each node. Node leases allow the kubelet to send heartbeats so that the control plane can detect node failure. kube-public This namespace is created automatically and is readable by all users (including those not authenticated). This namespace is mostly reserved for cluster usage, in case that some resources should be visible and readable publicly throughout the whole cluster. The public. title: Ingress - Kubernetes
description: Make your HTTP (or HTTPS) network service available using a protocol-aware configuration mechanism, that understands web concepts like URIs, hostnames, paths, and more.
content_summary: This resource for Ingress - Kubernetes (09. External Engineering, Protocols & Tools — Kubernetes, Containers & Cloud Native) details: Ingress Make your HTTP (or HTTPS) network service available using a protocol-aware configuration mechanism, that understands web concepts like URIs, hostnames, paths, and more. The Ingress concept lets you map traffic to different backends based on rules you define via the Kubernetes API. Feature state: Stable since Kubernetes v1.19 An API object that manages external access to the services in a cluster, typically HTTP. Ingress may provide load balancing, SSL termination and name-based virtual hosting. Note: The Kubernetes project recommends using Gateway instead of Ingress . The Ingress API has been frozen. This means that: The Ingress API is generally available, and is subject to the stability guarantees for generally available APIs. The Kubernetes project has no plans to remove Ingress from Kubernetes. The Ingress API is no longer being developed, and will have no further changes or updates made to it. Key commands and paths referenced in the article include: kubectl describe ingress ingress-resource-backend Name.
